topics.title: Length and Area Properties of Two-Dimensional Geometrical Figures
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: describe the length of two dimensional geometrical figures. (u)
develop, understand and state Pythagoras’ theorem (k u)
apply Pythagoras’ theorem to right angled and isosceles triangles. (u s)
understands the meaning of area in two dimensional geometrical figures (triangles, rectangles). (u s)

body.text: A farmer needs to know how much wire will go round a garden. A builder needs to know how much paint will cover a wall. A carpenter needs to know how long a roof rafter must be. These questions are about the length and area of flat shapes. In this topic you also meet Pythagoras’ theorem, one of the most useful facts in mathematics.

A two-dimensional (2D) figure is a flat shape, such as a triangle or a rectangle. The perimeter is the total length of its boundary. To find it, add the lengths of all the sides. Perimeter is measured in units of length, such as cm or m.

body.speech: The perimeter of a rectangle equals 2 times, l plus w

body.title: Fencing a garden
steps: Namubiru has a rectangular garden 12 m long and 8 m wide. She wants to put barbed wire around it once.
Barbed wire costs UGX 3,500 per metre at the hardware shop.

body.text: Area is the amount of flat surface a shape covers. We measure it by counting unit squares. A square with sides of 1 cm has an area of 1 square centimetre, written 1 cm². A rectangle 5 cm long and 3 cm wide holds 3 rows of 5 squares, so its area is 15 cm².

body.speech: The area of a rectangle equals l times w

body.text: Draw a rectangle around any triangle so that the base of the triangle is one side of the rectangle. The triangle covers exactly half of that rectangle. The height must be the perpendicular height. This is the distance from the top corner straight down to the base, at a right angle, not the length of a sloping side.

body.speech: The area of a triangle equals one half times base times perpendicular height

body.title: Painting the end wall of a house
steps: The end wall of a house is a rectangle 6 m wide and 3 m high, with a triangle on top. The triangle has a base of 6 m and a perpendicular height of 2 m.
Area of the rectangle = 6 × 3 = 18 m².
Area of the triangle = ½ × 6 × 2 = 6 m².
Total area = 18 + 6 = 24 m².
One litre of paint covers 8 m². Paint needed = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 litres.

body.text: A right-angled triangle has one angle of 90°. The longest side is opposite the right angle. It is called the hypotenuse. Pythagoras’ theorem links the three sides. The area of the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the areas of the squares on the other two sides.

body.speech: a squared plus b squared equals c squared, where c is the hypotenuse

body.text: Test it on a triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. The squares on the shorter sides have areas 9 cm² and 16 cm². Together they make 25 cm², which is the area of the square on the 5 cm side.

body.title: Show the theorem with paper triangles
body.text: Cut four identical right-angled triangles from scrap paper. Call the short sides a and b and the hypotenuse c. Draw a large square with sides of length a + b. First, place the four triangles inside it so that they leave a tilted square of side c in the middle. Then rearrange the same four triangles to leave two squares uncovered, one of side a and one of side b. The empty space is the same both times. Discuss in your group what this tells you about c², a² and b².

To find the hypotenuse, add the squares of the two shorter sides and take the square root. To find a shorter side, subtract the square of the known shorter side from the square of the hypotenuse, then take the square root.

body.title: Straight-line distance on a boda boda
steps: Kato rides a boda boda 8 km north and then 6 km east. How far is he from his starting point in a straight line?
The two roads meet at a right angle, so the straight-line distance is the hypotenuse c.

body.title: How high does the ladder reach?
steps: A ladder 5 m long leans against a wall. Its foot is 1.4 m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
The ladder is the hypotenuse, so c = 5 and one shorter side is 1.4. Call the height h.

body.text: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides. A line from the top corner straight down to the base cuts it into two identical right-angled triangles. This line also cuts the base exactly in half. So you can use Pythagoras’ theorem to find the height of an isosceles triangle.

body.title: The height of a roof
steps: Two roof rafters, each 2.6 m long, meet at the top. Their feet are 4.8 m apart. The triangle they make is isosceles.
The height cuts the 4.8 m base in half, giving 2.4 m on each side.
In one right-angled half, the hypotenuse is 2.6 m and the base is 2.4 m.
h = √1 = 1 m. The top of the roof is 1 m above the walls.
The area of the triangular gable = ½ × 4.8 × 1 = 2.4 m².

body.text: Builders often set out the corner of a house with string. They measure 3 m along one side, 4 m along the other, and move the strings until the distance between the ends is 5 m. Why does this give a perfect right angle?

Perimeter is the total length around a shape. Area is the surface it covers, in square units: a rectangle is l × w and a triangle is ½ × base × perpendicular height. In a right-angled triangle, a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse, the side opposite the right angle.
